methods.label: Apply the recurrence to the units digits
methods.explanation:
Only the units digits are needed. When two integers are added, their other digits contribute whole tens, so the new units digit is the units digit of the sum of the preceding two units digits.

Let \(d_n\) be the units digit of the \(n\)th Fibonacci term. Start with \(d_1=d_2=1\), add the preceding two digits, and keep only the units digit. For example, \(5+8=13\) gives the next digit \(3\). Continuing gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_1,\ldots,d_7&=1,1,2,3,5,8,3,\\
d_8,\ldots,d_{14}&=1,4,5,9,4,3,7,\\
d_{15},\ldots,d_{21}&=0,7,7,4,1,5,6.
\end{aligned}
\]
Before the final \(6\) in this list, the digits \(0,1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9\) have all appeared, while \(6\) has not. Thus \(6\) is the last of the ten digits to appear, and the answer is \(\boxed{6}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
